_source: Written only from Sweet Home 3D's own documentation: the package.html javadoc package descriptions in the application sources at SourceForge SVN revision r2382 (trunk/SweetHome3D/src, 2010-02-19, between releases 2.2 and 2.3), and the Plug-in developer's guide at http://www.sweethome3d.com/pluginDeveloperGuide.jsp as archived by the Wayback Machine on 2010-05-18 (sections 'Sweet Home 3D API - Javadoc', 'Model classes architecture', 'Plug-in classes architecture'); the README of that revision gives build instructions only. Package names, class names and file names were removed and replaced by plain descriptions.
sweetHome3DModel: Describes the model classes of Sweet Home 3D, the Model layer of its MVC (Model View Controller) architecture and the core upon which all the other parts depend: the home application entry point gives access to the user preferences (length unit, furniture catalog, textures catalog) and to the homes being edited, with their walls, furniture, rooms, dimension lines, labels and observer camera, and to how homes are read and written. Any modification of a model object is notified to displayed components with property change, collection and selection events; the model isn't thread safe.
sweetHome3DTools: Contains various tool classes useful in the View/Controller and IO parts, such as the classes implementing the content interface through which the model accesses external information like the icon and 3D model of a piece of furniture or the image of a texture.
sweetHome3DPlugin: Describes the super classes required to create Sweet Home 3D plug-ins: a plug-in may consist of one or more actions that are automatically added to the tool bar and menu bar of the home view. A plug-in manager created at application launch searches the plug-ins installed in the user's plug-ins folder and, each time a new home is edited, instantiates and configures a plug-in for each and retrieves its actions; plug-ins get an undoable edit support to post their modifications.
sweetHome3DViewController: Describes the controller classes and view interfaces of Sweet Home 3D; it controls the edition of the data stored by the model classes. The main home controller manages all the actions proposed to the end user and creates subcontrollers for the furniture catalog, home furniture, plan and so on, and all controllers create their associated view through an abstract view factory.
sweetHome3DSwing: Implements the views created by Sweet Home 3D controllers with Swing components; all these components are created on demand by a Swing view factory that implements the view factory interface specified by the view/controller layer.
sweetHome3DJava3D: Contains various 3D tool classes and 3D home objects useful in the Swing views.
sweetHome3DIO: Implements how to read and write the homes and user preferences created in the model classes of Sweet Home 3D: default user preferences are read from resources and written in local files and system preferences, and homes are read from and written to files.
sweetHome3DApplet: Instantiates the required classes to run Sweet Home 3D as an applet.
sweetHome3DApplication: Instantiates the required classes to run Sweet Home 3D as a stand-alone application: its main entry point creates a home application based on file-based user preferences, a home file recorder and the Swing views.
